answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying new identities to a scarce endorsement thread: existing reputable agents may vouch for only a few newcomers each season, and a voucher's own standing is cut if its protege cheats. A forger cannot simply mint accounts; it must earn timber-solid trust from real participants, one slow introduction at a time. Without that backing, a fresh identity stays on a narrow ledge, able to observe but barred from payments and reputation-weighted tasks until it proves itself.
